notes.meaning: On the ninth day, Abidan the leader of Benjamin brought his gifts to the tabernacle. Benjamin was camped on the west side, and the leaders presented their offerings in the exact order of their camps. His gifts included large silver dishes filled with grain and oil, as well as a gold dish filled with incense for God's holy table.

Abidan brought animals for burnt offerings, a sin offering, and peace offerings. Even during a joyful celebration, the sin offering reminded the people that they needed God's forgiveness. The large peace offering provided meat so the leaders and their friends could feast together in fellowship with the Lord.

On the tenth day, Ahiezer of the tribe of Dan brought his tribe's dedication gift. Dan was the leading tribe of the camp on the north side of the tabernacle. Even though Dan was one of the largest tribes, Ahiezer brought the exact same silver and gold vessels, showing that every tribe is equal before God.

Ahiezer offered clean animals for burnt, sin, and peace offerings. The burnt offering showed full commitment to God, while the peace offering celebrated peace with Him. These sacrifices showed that Dan joyfully joined all the other tribes in dedicating the altar.

On the eleventh day, Pagiel from the tribe of Asher brought his offering of silver and gold vessels. God gave each leader a separate day so that no tribe was rushed or overlooked. Taking time for each tribe showed that God took great delight in each act of worship.

Pagiel completed his tribe's dedication by presenting animals for burnt, sin, and peace offerings. Carrying out these sacrifices took a whole day of careful work by the priests. By recording every gift by name, God showed that He notices and remembers all faithful service.

On the twelfth day, Ahira the leader of Naphtali brought his offering before the Lord. Naphtali was the last tribe in the marching order, but their gift received the very same honor and attention. He presented the silver platter, the silver bowl, and the gold dish filled with incense.

Ahira brought the final set of animal sacrifices, completing the twelve days of dedication. Every tribe had now given an identical gift to honor God's altar. This demonstrated that all Israel shared an equal right and interest in the sacrifices offered to the Lord.

The text lists the total sum of all the silver gifts brought during the twelve days. There were twelve silver platters and twelve silver bowls, adding up to two thousand four hundred sanctuary shekels. Adding up the total showed how much wealth was freely given to furnish the tabernacle for God's glory.

The twelve gold dishes filled with incense weighed a total of one hundred and twenty shekels. These dishes held the sweet incense burned before God on the golden altar. God carefully recorded every ounce to show that He values the generous giving of His people.

The account lists the grand total of all the livestock sacrificed during the dedication. So many animals were brought because the valleys around Sinai had rich pasture to sustain large flocks and herds. The plentiful peace offerings provided a wonderful feast where the leaders and people celebrated their fellowship with God.

When Moses entered the Tent of Meeting, the Lord spoke to him in a clear, audible voice from above the mercy seat between the two cherubim. This fulfilled God's promise to meet with Moses and showed that He warmly accepted the gifts of the people. Christian teachers have long seen this voice as the eternal Word of God, who later became man to speak directly to us.
